items.stem: When does `context.Staff.Where(s => s.Active)` actually execute against the database?

options.text: Immediately, on the line where it is written
When the query is enumerated — e.g. .ToList(), foreach, .First()

items.explanation: LINQ-to-Entities uses deferred execution: the query runs when you enumerate it (ToList/foreach/First), not when it is defined.

misconceptions.a: Defining the query only builds it; enumeration triggers the SQL.

items.stem: In a feed's `LoadEntities()`, what is the role of `.Select(s => new Staff { ... })`?

options.text: It deletes rows from the source
It projects each source row into a Staff POCO
It writes the Staff records to the destination

items.explanation: The Select projects source rows into the entity POCO type the feed returns as its snapshot.

misconceptions.c: Writing to the destination is the sink's job; the feed only reads and projects.

items.stem: Why does `StaffFeed.LoadEntities()` call `.ToList()` at the end of the query?

options.text: To materialize the results (run the SQL) and return a concrete snapshot collection
It is optional and has no effect

items.explanation: ToList() forces enumeration, executing the query and producing an in-memory collection — the snapshot the feed returns.

misconceptions.d: Without materializing, the query could execute lazily after the context is disposed, causing errors.

items.stem: Why is it a good idea to materialize a query (`.ToList()`) before doing complex C# transformations on the results?
rubric: EF tries to translate LINQ to SQL; complex/unsupported C# inside the query can fail to translate or run inefficiently
Materializing first brings the rows into memory so subsequent C# runs client-side (and after that the context can be safely disposed)
items.sampleAnswer: EF translates the query to SQL, and arbitrary C# in the middle either can't be translated or runs server-side unexpectedly. Calling .ToList() first pulls the rows into memory, so any complex transformation runs as plain in-memory C# — and you're not depending on the DbContext still being open.
